name: SQLAlchemy
description: Typed SQLAlchemy 2.0 with Alembic migrations on PostgreSQL, for FastAPI.

specSections.title: Data Model & Migrations
specSections.guidance: For each entity/table: columns with types, lengths and numeric precision, nullability and defaults; the primary key (UUIDv7 or identity); foreign keys with an explicit on-delete behaviour; unique indexes from business rules (say which are case-insensitive); check constraints; indexes for foreign keys and query predicates; enums stored as strings; UTC timestamps; and which aggregates are edited concurrently and need a concurrency token (409 CONFLICT). Then the migration plan: one migration per change, named, in order, with which steps are expand/contract (add, backfill, switch code, drop later) so the previous version keeps working during rollout; any data backfill; the reference/seed data (dev-only seed per role and state); and how migrations run in each environment (alembic upgrade head in the API image as the platform's pre-deploy step, or the build step gated by AIDE_RUN_MIGRATIONS on Vercel).

order.reason: Migrations come before the services and routers that use their tables.

exclusive.reason: The data engineer owns models and migrations, not routers or Pydantic DTOs.

protectedPaths.reason: Alembic revisions on the base commit are immutable (FR-125); a schema change is a new revision.

generatedFiles.ciCheck: uv run alembic upgrade head && uv run alembic check && test "$(uv run alembic heads | wc -l)" -eq 1 (against the CI Postgres service)

requiredEnv.description: PostgreSQL connection for the API and Alembic. Settings normalises postgres:// and postgresql:// to postgresql+asyncpg:// and adds ssl=require for managed hosts. On Vercel use the Supabase transaction pooler (:6543) with NullPool and statement_cache_size=0.

checklist.item: Exactly one new migration per schema change, never an edit to a migration that exists on the base commit.
Breaking changes (rename, drop, type change) use expand/contract so the previous version runs against the new schema during preview and production rollout.
Columns are explicit (lengths, precision, nullability), foreign keys have a deliberate on-delete, and every foreign key and query predicate is indexed.
Uniqueness rules from the spec are unique indexes or constraints (case-insensitive where the spec says so), and concurrently edited aggregates have a concurrency token mapped to 409 CONFLICT.
Timestamps are UTC (timestamptz/datetimeoffset) from an injected clock, and enums are stored as strings.
Integration tests run against the real engine in a container with every migration applied; no in-memory or SQLite substitute.
Queries are parameterised, project only the needed columns, paginate lists and avoid N+1.
The seed is idempotent, dev-only and gated; reference data is part of the migrations.
No Base.metadata.create_all() in app code; alembic upgrade head is the one-off pre-start migrate step.
Revisions chain from the single current head (down_revision), have a working downgrade where practical, and renames are alter_column, not drop plus add.
Models are typed 2.0 (Mapped/mapped_column) on a Base with a constraint naming convention; relationships use lazy="raise" with explicit loaders in async code.
